ai.definition: Swarm Micro-Bots are a collection of thousands of millimeter-scale robots that work together in swarms to accomplish complex tasks through stigmergic communication and decentralized control.
ai.howItWorks: Micro-bots communicate with each other via stigmergy, leaving signals or markers in their environment which influence the behavior of nearby bots. They operate under decentralized control algorithms allowing them to coordinate without a central command structure.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing tasks that require precise manipulation at small scales and complexity beyond what can be achieved by single large-scale robots.
ai.manufacturing: Manufactured using microfabrication techniques, including lithography and MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems) processes.
ai.buildProcess: Design, fabrication of individual bots, assembly into swarms, programming for swarm behavior, testing and calibration.
ai.costDrivers: High precision manufacturing, complex software development, energy efficiency requirements, miniaturization challenges.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Emerging technology with growing potential but not yet widely deployed in commercial applications.
ai.regulation: No specific regulations currently exist; will likely require new standards for safety and efficacy as the technology matures.
ai.risks: Technical challenges, regulatory hurdles, ethical concerns around deployment, environmental impact of manufacturing process.
ai.profitability: Uncertain due to current lack of widespread adoption but could become highly profitable with successful commercialization in key sectors like healthcare and environmental remediation.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected advancements in materials science for miniaturization, improved communication protocols, enhanced autonomy and coordination algorithms.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking.

glossary.def: A method of indirect communication where the state of a shared environment influences the behavior of individuals, leading them to modify that environment in turn.
Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems, which are microscopic devices combining mechanical elements, sensors, actuators, and electronics on a single substrate through microfabrication technology.

subsystems.name: Individual micro-robot
subsystems.role: the physical agent; at millimetre scale it must pack locomotion, sensing, power and communication into a tiny package.

subsystems.name: Communication and local sensing
subsystems.role: lets robots interact without a central controller, using stigmergy or short-range signals.

subsystems.name: Decentralized control
subsystems.role: software that turns simple local rules into collective behaviour.

subsystems.name: Power and energy
subsystems.role: supplies energy for movement and computation; often the limiting factor.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing and assembly
subsystems.role: how thousands of identical micro-robots are made affordably.

subsystems.name: Swarm-level actuation
subsystems.role: the mechanisms that move the collective, such as magnetic fields, acoustic waves or chemical gradients.

buildSteps.title: Design the individual robot
buildSteps.detail: Choose a locomotion method (magnetic, acoustic, chemical, or vibration), define sensor and communication needs, and specify size and materials.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate micro-components
buildSteps.detail: Use microfabrication to make actuators, sensors, and circuitry on silicon or polymer substrates; some parts may be printed or moulded.

buildSteps.title: Assemble robots
buildSteps.detail: Pick-and-place or self-assembly aligns and bonds layers into complete robots; for thousands, parallel batch methods are needed.

buildSteps.title: Program collective behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Write decentralized algorithms where each robot follows local rules; stigmergy (leaving traces in the environment) can coordinate without direct communication.

buildSteps.title: Test in controlled environments
buildSteps.detail: Release swarms in lab arenas with tracking cameras to validate aggregation, transport, or pattern formation.

buildSteps.title: Scale production
buildSteps.detail: Develop high-throughput manufacturing to make thousands of robots with consistent properties.

buildSteps.title: Deploy for applications
buildSteps.detail: For medicine, robots must be biocompatible and externally controllable; for environmental cleanup, they must operate in water or soil and be retrievable or biodegradable.

buildSteps.title: Ensure safety and control
buildSteps.detail: Design fail-safes, off-switches, and methods to remove or degrade robots after use.

prerequisites.why: the semiconductor industry already makes microscopic devices, but integrating actuators and power at millimetre scale is harder.
millimetre-scale batteries exist but store little energy; harvesting from magnetic fields or light is being researched.
short-range radio and infrared links exist, but power and size constraints limit range and bandwidth.
simulations and centimetre-scale robots (like Kilobots) have demonstrated collective behaviours, but not yet at millimetre scale with thousands.
some materials are safe for the body, but combining them with electronics and actuators is a challenge.

pathway.milestone: laboratory swarms of centimetre-scale robots (hundreds) demonstrating aggregation, transport, and pattern formation
pathway.unlocks: proven algorithms and understanding of collective behaviour.

pathway.milestone: millimetre-scale robots produced in batches of thousands, with basic locomotion and communication
pathway.unlocks: larger-scale experiments and early environmental sensing applications.

pathway.milestone: in vivo medical trials with small swarms for targeted drug delivery or localised treatment
deployment for environmental cleanup, such as oil-spill remediation or water treatment, with biodegradable robots
pathway.unlocks: scalable, low-impact cleanup of contaminated sites.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous swarms for complex tasks in medicine and industry
pathway.unlocks: new capabilities in microsurgery, manufacturing, and environmental monitoring.
